claims.claim: Preserved all seven original registry bodies byte-exact and added separately pinned tca-2 v2 and roa-1-r3 v3 identities. Registry limits admit nine recognized identities within 57344 bytes while retaining exact version, digest and duplicate checks.

TCA-2 retains five construct checks, six adversarial checks and one closure, requiring bounded source API, historical test and modification-authority challenges; missing decisive sources require UNKNOWN and NO_DECISION.

Added a TASK-391 r1 regression covering published direct codec imports, the historical AST restriction and inspect-only test scope; unresolved blockers prevent candidate exposure and cannot be erased by a later clear pass.

ROA-1 R3 retains five checks and one closure, distinguishes execution, verification and completion causes, and requires full original acceptance for readiness. Completion-only fixtures for RUN-391-013 and RUN-383-002 select a completion lever, while a genuine code regression permits CODE_FIX; instructions preserve acceptance, sticky Executor and Runtime completion authority.

Extended the existing canonical authenticator to recognize one separate successor approval bound to preserved historical approval and independently reviewed publication. Defaults remain historical without that authority, and canonical movement stops admitted continuation without switching profiles.

Added focused digest, partial/mixed/forged/stale policy, reviewed-body, ordinary default caller and continuation tests, including unchanged Human V1 option coverage through the existing authentication path.

Documentation identifies historical and successor profiles and digests, states that successors are not automatically activated, and describes later Human/Brain approval and reviewed publication without asserting live correctness, verification or performance.
